answer: A sybil operator's advantage is doing one piece of work and wearing many masks to praise it. Split every reward claim across a ridge: two isolated panels judge it blind, never seeing each other's verdict. Only concordance pays — the same opal colour glimpsed from two separate angles. A farm must then do genuine work twice, in isolation, without leaking a tell between its own masks; identical phrasing across the divide betrays a single author, and each panel's independent pulse of judgment makes self-praise worthless unless strangers agree.
